answer: To resist Sybil swarms, nodes anchor identities to a cryptographic attestation chain verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Valid agents anchor trust within a secure reef registry, while unverified identities quarantine in a restricted lagoon. Interconnected agents form a trellis network requiring superlinear collateral scaling: registering N clone identities imposes an exponential capital exhaustion cost O(2^N) to deter attackers.
